taxpayer.notes: Widower living in Schenectady, NY; daughter Lata Kapoor (married to Pedro Escamilla since April 2014) and her children lived with him from March 2015. All dollar amounts rounded to nearest dollar.

adjustments: disallowed dependency exemptions for I.M.E. and P.A.E.
disallowed head of household filing status
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Dependency exemptions, HOH status, ACTC and EIC based on grandchildren
conceded: Respondent conceded petitioner is not liable for the 6662(a) penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Daughter Lata Kapoor and minor child I.M.E. moved into petitioner's home in March 2015 and remained the rest of the year
findings_of_fact.snippet: In March 2015 Ms. Kapoor and her minor child I.M.E. moved from Chicago, Illinois, to Schenectady to live with petitioner.

findings_of_fact.fact: P.A.E. born fall 2015 (Chicago, two-week trip) and lived with petitioner and Ms. Kapoor for remainder of year
findings_of_fact.snippet: P.A.E. was born in fall 2015 and lived with petitioner and Ms. Kapoor for the remainder of the year.

findings_of_fact.fact: Ms. Kapoor married to Pedro Escamilla since April 2014; petitioner unaware
findings_of_fact.snippet: Although Ms. Kapoor had been married to Mr. Escamilla since April 2014, petitioner was unaware of their marriage.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner paid all rent and utilities, clothes, phone and cable
findings_of_fact.snippet: During his daughter’s stay in his home, petitioner paid all rent and utilities.

findings_of_fact.fact: Original return AGI $11,679; Form 1040X (April 2017) added $5,100 self-employment income, AGI $15,545
findings_of_fact.snippet: the additional income resulted in an adjusted gross income of $15,545 as reported on petitioner’s 2015 Form 1040X.

findings_of_fact.fact: Ms. Kapoor and spouse jointly filed 2015 Form 1040 in April 2016 claiming I.M.E. and P.A.E. for dependency, ACTC and EIC
findings_of_fact.snippet: The couple claimed their children, I.M.E. and P.A.E., as dependents for purposes of dependency exemption deductions, the additional child tax credit, and the EIC.

findings_of_fact.fact: Children satisfy qualifying-child tests as to both petitioner (grandparent) and Ms. Kapoor (parent); minors, not self-supporting, unmarried
findings_of_fact.snippet: they had the same principal place of abode as both petitioner and Ms. Kapoor for more than one-half the year

findings_of_fact.fact: 2015 completed phaseout amount for no qualifying children $14,820 (Rev. Proc. 2014-61); petitioner AGI and earned income exceeded it
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner’s adjusted gross income and earned income both exceeded the phaseout amount of $14,820 for 2015.
On August 1, 2017, respondent issued a notice of deficiency to petitioner for the year in issue.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to dependency exemptions for grandchildren I.M.E. and P.A.E. when their mother, living in the same household, also claimed them?
issues.holding: No; under the §152(c)(4)(A)(i) tie-breaker the children are qualifying children of their parent, and they cannot be qualifying relatives because they are qualifying children of another taxpayer
issues.computable_reason: Mechanical tie-breaker: parent claimed children, so parent prevails

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to head of household filing status for 2015?
issues.holding: No; no qualifying child or dependent

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the additional child tax credit for I.M.E. and P.A.E.?
Is petitioner entitled to the EIC (with two qualifying children, or alternatively with none)?
issues.holding: No; children not his qualifying children, and AGI/earned income ($15,545 amended) exceeds $14,820 completed phaseout for no-child EIC

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioner as to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a).
decision.summary: Deficiency sustained in full (no dependency exemptions, HOH, ACTC or EIC); penalty conceded by respondent

notes: Burden of proof played no role (facts clearly established via daughter's joint return and transcript). Petitioner's lack of knowledge of daughter's marriage/joint return irrelevant to eligibility. Court did not address §152(b)(1)/(c)(1)(E) issues for the daughter; tie-breaker applied directly. Birth year of I.M.E. not stated (minor).
